overall: The AG found the Committee violated the Open Meeting Law by posting the March 7, 2014 notice late and without topics, and by posting no notice for the April 4 and April 11, 2014 meetings; the May 27 re-vote did not cure these. Ordered future compliance only.

allegations.summary: Complaint alleged notice failures; the March 7, 2014 meeting notice was filed at 2:48 PM on March 5, less than 48 hours before the meeting.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee posted notice for its March 7, 2014 11:00 AM meeting at 2:48 PM on March 5, 2014.

allegations.summary: The March 7, 2014 notice listed only the date, time and place and no topics for discussion.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, this notice did not comply with the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: No notice was posted at all for the April 4, 2014 meeting, which considered eight OPM proposals and declined four proposers.
allegations.key_passage: The Committee did not post any notice for its April 4, 2014 or its April 11, 2014 meetings.

allegations.summary: No notice was posted for the April 11, 2014 meeting, where proposers were interviewed and a conditional contract was awarded.
allegations.key_passage: This was a clear violation of the Open Meeting Law.

allegations.summary: Committee argued its May 27, 2014 re-evaluation and re-vote cured the missing notices for April 4 and April 11.
allegations.key_passage: its discussion during the May 27, 2014 meeting was not sufficient to fully address its failure to post notices for its April 4, 2014 and April 11, 2014 meetings.

remedy: Immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law.
note: Read by a language model from the letter; every key passage is checked verbatim against it and dropped if not. A holding is the Attorney General’s reading of the law in this case only.
